articles.body: Call of Cthulhu: Old Ones Origins , an asymmetrical tactical board game developed by Chaosium Inc. and based on H.P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos, has been canceled. On Nov. 15, Chaosium posted a message on the project's updates page on tabletop crowdfunding platform Gamefound explaining that the game's designer, Samuel William Bailey, was convicted in Skagit County, Washington on Friday, Nov. 13, of multiple counts of first-degree rape of a minor and child molestation.

articles.title: Why Passport Photos Fail Online: 6 Image Checks Every Photo Tool Should Perform
articles.excerpt: A passport photo can look perfectly fine on a phone screen and still fail an online application. Because image quality is only one part of the process. Digital passport photos must also meet specific…
articles.body: A passport photo can look perfectly fine on a phone screen and still fail an online application. Because image quality is only one part of the process. Digital passport photos must also meet specific requirements for dimensions, facial positioning, background, lighting and file quality. For anyone building an image-processing application—or preparing a passport photo—understanding these checks can prevent unnecessary rejections and repeated uploads. Let's break down six important checks. 1. Image dimensions and cropping A photo may have excellent clarity but still be rejected if its dimensions or aspect ratio do not match the required specification. An image-processing tool should: Check the uploaded image dimensions. Apply the required aspect ratio.

articles.title: The AI Pair Programmer Illusion: How AI Is Eroding Developers’ Core Skills
articles.excerpt: I watched a junior developer spend twenty minutes trying to fix a null pointer exception last week. Not because the bug was hard—it wasn’t. Because they’d never debugged one without an AI assistant su…
articles.body: I watched a junior developer spend twenty minutes trying to fix a null pointer exception last week. Not because the bug was hard—it wasn’t. Because they’d never debugged one without an AI assistant suggesting the fix. They kept waiting for the ghost in the machine to tell them what to do. It didn’t. So they sat there, stuck, staring at a stack trace like it was written in Latin. That’s when it hit me: We’re not building 10x developers. We’re building developers who can’t work without a copilot. The pitch for AI pair programming is intoxicating. Type a comment, get a function. Describe a bug, get a patch. Autocomplete on steroids. And sure, for boilerplate and syntax lookup, it’s genuinely useful.
articles.author: Om Keswani

articles.title: Voice AI Is Easy. Making It Talk to Your Database Is the Actual Job
articles.excerpt: Quick Summary (Key Takeaway): According to the India Voice AI Readiness 2026 report by Nasscom and Krisp, 61% of companies cut customer interaction costs by over 20% using Voice AI. However, only 13%…
articles.body: Quick Summary (Key Takeaway): According to the India Voice AI Readiness 2026 report by Nasscom and Krisp , 61% of companies cut customer interaction costs by over 20% using Voice AI. However, only 13% have scaled it across multiple customer journeys. Banking & Finance leads adoption overall (~34% share) , followed by Telecom (~27%), Retail (~22%), and Logistics (~14%), because their calls rely on structured database lookups (balances, billing queries, order tracking). To successfully scale into 2027, teams must connect voice agents to live CRM and billing databases with sub-300ms APIs, test for noisy acoustic environments and regional accents, build smooth human handoffs, and track problems resolved rather than raw calls answered.

articles.body: Audio stem separation has improved dramatically over the past few years, largely driven by open-source deep learning architectures like Demucs from Meta AI. If you want to isolate clean vocals from a track or strip them away to create an instrumental backing, the results from models like htdemucs (Hybrid Transformer Demucs) are genuinely impressive. However, running these tools out of the box is strictly a terminal-bound workflow. You have to clone a repository, set up a Python virtual environment, configure PyTorch and CUDA drivers, and run terminal commands with custom parameter flags. For non-technical musicians, producers, or colleagues who just need an isolated vocal track for a demo, the terminal is an unnecessary barrier.

articles.title: Why Coding Agents Still Fail The Same Way Every Time - And What I Did Instead
articles.excerpt: Coding agents don't fail because they can't type code. They fail because they call the wrong tool, read the wrong error, try again the same wrong way, and get stuck. I watched that happen over and ove…
articles.body: Coding agents don't fail because they can't type code. They fail because they call the wrong tool, read the wrong error, try again the same wrong way, and get stuck. I watched that happen over and over in real coding sessions. So I built something to fix it. What MegaBit is MegaBit is a data factory. I pick a real open source bug. I revert the fix. I let an agent fix it live inside a sandbox, and I record every command it runs. When the agent's fix breaks its own tests, I keep the failure in the data. When it passes, I keep the patch. That way the model learns the real path: the wrong turns , the bad tool calls , the recovery , not just the finished diff.

articles.body: Field surveying sits at the intersection of physical environments, hardware integration and mathematical precision. Traditional total stations provide reliable surveying capabilities, but their workflows can remain disconnected from modern cloud-based GIS systems. On the other hand, mobile surveying applications often struggle with sensor noise, unstable orientation readings and limited integration with professional surveying workflows. GeoSight is an attempt to bridge this gap. It is a mobile Total Station and Spatial GIS platform designed to bring optical sighting, sensor-based orientation, external measurement hardware, RTK GNSS positioning and enterprise GIS integration into a unified field workflow. articles.body: TL;DR Fifteen guests at a hotel in Germany were reportedly hurt after a faulty dosing system pumped too much chlorine into the hotel pool. The pool’s safety system sent a warning by email, but staff never received it because of last week’s global Microsoft 365 outage. Microsoft says the outage was caused by a problem from an earlier network capacity upgrade, and it has promised a full post-incident report. Last week’s Microsoft 365 outage did more than keep people out of their inboxes. In Germany it played a part in a chemical incident that sent hotel guests to the hospital. German public broadcaster WDR reported that on Friday, November 13, a fault in the automatic chlorine dosing system at Hotel Ling Bao pushed far too much chlorine into the hotel’s pool.

articles.title: NASA's interstellar Voyager 1 probe is about to reach 1 light-day from Earth after nearly 50 years in space
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth. NASA's long-running interstellar Voyager 1 probe will mark one light-day of distance from Earth on Nov. 18, when the spacecraft is 49 years, two months and 11 days old. The agency recently stated the record distance, which will be reached at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (101607 GMT) is "a huge milestone by any measure, and a day worth celebrating." During the light-day crossover, Voyager will be in contact with the Madrid station of the three-antenna Deep Space Network that monitors all deep-space missions. The spacecraft is currently making its way through the constellation Ophiuchus from the perspective of Earth, said Jeffrey Hayes, a NASA official whose work includes Voyager 1.

According to Entertainment Weekly , Ebenezer had a $38 million production budget, though that does not include the film's additional marketing and promotional costs. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001.

articles.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
articles.excerpt: "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon. Everyone is very confident on this."
articles.body: For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold.
